text:
These Academic Regulations establish the general rules governing undergraduate academic activity at Northbridge Institute of Technology (NIT). They cover registration, attendance, examinations, grading, academic progression, revaluation, supplementary examinations, academic records, and appeals. They apply to students enrolled in undergraduate programmes unless a programme-specific regulation expressly states otherwise. A programme-specific rule should be read together with these general regulations rather than assumed to replace every general requirement.

The purpose of the regulations is to provide predictable procedures while allowing the Institute to handle exceptional circumstances through designated authorities. Students are responsible for reading published notices and retaining documents relevant to their academic status.

The academic year normally consists of two regular semesters and an optional summer term. The Academic Office publishes the academic calendar before registration. The calendar identifies instructional periods, examination periods, registration windows, and major administrative deadlines.

A timetable may be modified for operational reasons. When the Academic Office publishes a revised timetable, students should use the revised date for the activity identified in the notice. A timetable change does not by itself change eligibility rules.

Students must register for courses during the registration period. During the first ten instructional days, a student may add a course with approval from the course instructor and department office. After the add period, changes require the approvals specified by the Academic Office.

A student may not normally register for a course whose listed prerequisite has not been completed. A department may approve a documented prerequisite waiver where the programme procedure permits one. A waiver must be recorded before the student is treated as satisfying the prerequisite.

Students should review their registration after the add/drop period. Errors should be reported promptly because an unrecorded registration can affect examination eligibility and academic records.

Students are expected to attend lectures, laboratories, tutorials, seminars, and other compulsory academic activities. The standard minimum attendance requirement for appearing in a semester-end examination is **75% of scheduled instructional sessions in the course**.

Attendance is calculated separately for each course. Attendance from one course cannot be transferred to another course. The departmental attendance record is the primary administrative record unless corrected through the prescribed process.

Students below the standard threshold may submit an attendance representation within five working days after publication of the shortage list. The representation should identify the course, recorded percentage, dates or circumstances relied upon, and supporting evidence. Filing a representation does not automatically restore eligibility.

Approved institute-representative activities, officially assigned academic activities, and other absences specifically recognized by an institutional notice may be treated according to the instructions applicable to that activity.

Students should verify that approved adjustments have been reflected in the departmental record. An approval for one activity should not be assumed to apply to a different activity or course.

Medical attendance requests are handled under the Medical and Exceptional Circumstances Policy. Students must follow the medical documentation and approval process. For semester-end examination eligibility, the general 75% attendance threshold in Section 4 applies to all students, including students whose medical documentation has been approved; this regulation does not create a lower medical attendance threshold.

A student who satisfies the applicable attendance requirement, has valid course registration, and meets other published prerequisites is ordinarily eligible to sit for the semester-end examination. Departments may publish an eligibility list before examinations.

A student whose name is absent from an eligibility list should contact the department before the deadline in the relevant notice. The department may verify attendance, registration, and approved exceptions before correcting the list.

A student who misses an examination because of an approved medical emergency may request a deferred or make-up examination. The request should normally be submitted within three working days after the missed examination and should include the documentation requested by the Academic Office.

The standard examination-absence provision does not expressly establish an automatic right to a deferred examination for family weddings, vacations, ordinary personal travel, or social events. Students should not infer eligibility from the existence of medical absence procedures.

Students must carry the identification and materials specified in the examination notice. Unauthorized electronic devices, communication with other candidates, unauthorized material, impersonation, or deliberate disruption may constitute examination misconduct.

Invigilators may record incidents and refer them to the Academic Integrity Committee. A student may be required to provide a statement about an alleged incident.

A course grade is determined using the assessment scheme approved for the course. The scheme may include assignments, laboratory work, quizzes, projects, mid-semester examinations, and a final examination. The syllabus should identify the weighting of major components.

Grades are recorded according to the Institute's grading scale. A student should review published results and report a suspected administrative error through the prescribed process.

Students must satisfy the minimum passing requirement for each registered course. Programme progression may depend on credits completed, failed courses, prerequisite relationships, and any progression conditions published for the programme.

A failed course may need to be repeated when required by the programme. The existence of a supplementary examination does not automatically mean that every failed course qualifies.

Where a revaluation facility is offered, students may submit a request through the prescribed portal or office within the published period. The request should identify the course and examination.

Revaluation is a review mechanism and does not guarantee an increase in marks. If the Institute permits a correction for an administrative error, the corrected record should be reflected through the official result process.

The Institute may offer supplementary examinations for specified courses or categories of students. The relevant examination notice establishes eligibility, registration, fee requirements, and dates.

Students should not assume that a supplementary examination is available for every failed course or every semester. The published notice controls the particular offering.

A student may appeal an academic decision when an applicable regulation provides an appeal route. The appeal should identify the decision, course or examination, date, grounds, and supporting documentation.

An appellate authority may uphold a decision, modify it within its authority, or return it to the original office for reconsideration. An appeal does not automatically suspend an academic deadline unless the applicable procedure says so.

The Academic Committee may issue interpretations of academic regulations and may approve limited exceptions where an applicable policy expressly grants that authority. The existence of a committee does not by itself mean that every academic requirement can be waived.

Committee decisions should identify the matter considered and any relief granted. A decision for one student should not automatically be treated as a general amendment to the regulations.

The Academic Office maintains official academic records. Students should use the designated process to request corrections. Supporting documents may be required.

Unofficial screenshots or messages should not be treated as a replacement for an official record when a formal procedure requires the official record.

Official academic notices are published through the student portal or another channel designated by the Academic Office. A notice changing a date should identify the activity and applicable academic period.

Students are responsible for monitoring notices relevant to their programme. When two notices appear inconsistent, the student should request clarification from the responsible office rather than choose a provision solely because it is more favorable.

A working day is a day on which the Institute's administrative offices are open. Weekends and officially declared institutional holidays are not normally working days unless a notice expressly states otherwise.
Students are responsible for monitoring registration, attendance, examination eligibility, results, and deadlines. Students should retain evidence of approved requests and official decisions.

A programme may publish additional requirements for laboratories, clinical work, internships, projects, or professional accreditation. Such requirements must be communicated through an official programme document or notice.

These regulations provide a general academic framework. Where an official policy expressly grants a different procedure for a defined category, that provision should be read in its stated context. Where two applicable provisions appear incompatible and no precedence rule resolves them, students should seek an institutional determination.

Students enrolled in programmes containing internships, capstone projects, laboratories, or fieldwork must satisfy the requirements published by the relevant department. A project deadline is not automatically extended because another course has granted an exception. Students should obtain written approval when an approved academic activity changes their expected participation.

Instructors may publish course materials and announcements through the learning platform designated by the Institute. Students are responsible for checking the platform during the teaching period. An informal message from another student is not an official amendment to an academic regulation.

When a student believes an attendance entry is incorrect, the student should identify the course, date, and disputed session. The department may compare attendance registers and approved adjustment records. A correction should be recorded in the official attendance system when accepted.

The examination timetable identifies the course, date, time, and venue. Students must verify the final published timetable before each examination. A student who relies on an obsolete timetable may still be required to follow the final official schedule unless the Institute determines otherwise.

Permitted materials are determined by the examination notice or course instructions. A material permitted in one examination should not automatically be assumed to be permitted in another. Students should ask the department when an instruction is unclear.

Official results are released through the designated academic channel. Transcripts contain the academic record maintained by the Institute. Students should report discrepancies promptly and provide evidence supporting a requested correction.

Graduation requires completion of the credits and programme requirements applicable to the student's programme. Students should verify outstanding requirements with the department before the graduation application deadline. Attendance, examination, fee, and conduct requirements may each have separate consequences under their applicable policies.

A formal academic leave of absence may be available where an applicable programme or Institute process provides for it. Informal absence from classes should not be treated as an approved leave of absence. A student returning from approved leave must complete the re-entry procedure.

Students must use the identification method specified by the Institute for examinations and selected administrative processes. A lost identification card should be reported promptly. The procedure for temporary identification is determined by the responsible office.

When a student submits an academic request, the student should retain the acknowledgement, reference number, and final decision where provided. If no response is received by a published deadline, the student should contact the office identified in the procedure rather than assume approval.

An answer generated from these regulations must distinguish a general rule from a conditional exception. A conditional exception should not be applied to a student who does not satisfy its stated conditions. Conversely, a general rule should not be presented as absolute when an expressly applicable exception exists.

Where the available documents do not establish a clear answer, students should be directed to the responsible institutional authority. The Institute's regulations are intended to support administration, not to authorize students or automated systems to invent precedence rules.
Students are responsible for paying tuition, hostel, examination, and other applicable fees by the deadlines published by the Institute.
For this evaluation corpus, the baseline semester-fee deadline is **15 August**. The fee schedule below is the controlling table within this document.

| Fee Type | Due Date | Standard Late Fee |
|---|---|---:|
| Semester Fee | 15 August | ₹500 |
| Hostel Fee | 20 August | ₹300 |
| Examination Fee | 10 November | ₹200 |
| Library Deposit | 15 August | ₹100 |
| Student Activity Fee | 25 August | ₹100 |
A late fee may be charged when payment is made after the applicable deadline. Students should retain payment confirmation.

If an online payment is debited but not reflected in the student account, the student should submit the transaction reference through the designated support channel. A payment-failure report does not automatically cancel a valid fee deadline.
Refunds are governed by the applicable withdrawal and refund schedule. Some administrative fees may be non-refundable.
Installment payment is available only when expressly approved. An installment approval should state the amounts and dates.
Fee waivers may be granted only under a published scheme or authorized decision. Financial difficulty alone does not automatically create a waiver.
Unpaid fees may result in an administrative hold where an Institute notice provides for such a hold. A hold may affect registration or access to selected services.
Students who believe a fee has been incorrectly charged should contact the Finance Office with supporting records. Corrections are considered after verification.
The Finance Office may publish revised schedules. Students should check the latest official notice for the applicable academic period.
Students should retain digital or printed payment receipts. A receipt should show the transaction reference and amount where available.

A payment made by a parent, sponsor, or other third party remains associated with the student's account when correctly identified. Students should verify that the payer uses the correct account information.
This document provides baseline fee rules for the evaluation corpus. Where a later official notice expressly changes a deadline, the notice should be considered together with this policy.

Students should use only payment channels designated by the Institute. They should not share payment credentials or one-time passwords with another person. The Finance Office will not treat a private message as an official payment instruction.
If a student pays the same fee twice, the student should submit both transaction references. The Finance Office may verify the transactions before processing a correction or refund.
A transaction marked failed by the payment gateway may still require verification if the student's bank account was debited. Students should provide the transaction reference and payment date.
Students may request official fee receipts or certificates through the designated Finance Office process. The request should contain sufficient account information for verification.
Where an external sponsor pays a student's fee, the sponsor should follow the payment identification procedure. Sponsorship does not automatically alter the student's liability for a valid fee.
A student should complete fee payment and registration steps specified for the relevant academic period. A payment issue should be reported promptly when it prevents registration.

A revised fee notice should identify the academic period, fee category, and effective date. Students should compare the notice with the baseline policy and seek clarification when the two cannot be reconciled.

The fee policy describes baseline procedures, but an evaluation system should never silently choose between two incompatible deadlines. It should expose conflicting evidence and state that the corpus does not provide an unambiguous resolution.

This handbook establishes residence rules for students living in Institute hostels. It covers room allocation, entry, visitors, leave, common facilities, safety, discipline, maintenance, and emergency procedures.

Accommodation is subject to availability and the allocation procedure. Students must complete residence forms and provide accurate emergency contact information. Allocation may consider programme year and other criteria published by the Hostel Office.
Rooms are assigned by the Hostel Office. Students may request a room change during the published request period. A change is effective only after approval and update of the hostel record.
The standard hostel curfew is **10:00 PM**. Residents returning after curfew must use the designated late-entry process and may be required to provide a reason.
Students arriving after curfew must register their arrival. Repeated late entries may result in a warning or referral to the Hostel Discipline Committee.

Visitors may enter only during published visiting hours and must register at the security desk. Overnight visitors are not permitted unless the Hostel Office grants written authorization under the applicable residence procedure.
Residents leaving campus overnight must submit the prescribed leave request. Approval may depend on residence arrangements and programme requirements.
Residents must follow mess timings and hygiene requirements. Special dietary requests may be submitted to hostel administration but depend on feasibility and available facilities.
Students are responsible for reasonable care of assigned rooms and furniture. Damage beyond ordinary wear may be charged to the responsible resident after assessment.

Unauthorized dangerous items, harassment, deliberate property damage, unauthorized commercial activity, and conduct that materially disturbs residents are prohibited. Serious matters may be referred to the Institute disciplinary process.
Only appliances identified as permitted by the Hostel Office may be used. High-load appliances may be prohibited for electrical safety.
Students should check academic and hostel schedules before requesting leave during examination periods. Hostel approval does not change academic examination requirements.
During a verified emergency, security staff may temporarily modify entry procedures. An emergency measure should be recorded and does not permanently change the standard curfew.
Warnings, fines, restrictions, or referral may be imposed depending on the seriousness and recurrence of conduct. Students should receive information about the applicable process.
A student may appeal a hostel disciplinary decision when the applicable notice or process provides an appeal route.
Residents should maintain quiet during designated study and sleeping periods. Repeated disturbance may be treated as a residence conduct issue.
Special residence arrangements may be announced for Institute events. Such notices should identify the dates and temporary visitor arrangements.
Students should carry their residence identification when required. Lost identification should be reported to the Hostel Office or security desk.
Fire exits and emergency equipment must remain unobstructed. Students must follow evacuation instructions during drills and emergencies.
Lost property found in common areas should be handed to the designated hostel office or security desk. Students claiming an item may be asked to provide identifying information.

Authorized staff may inspect rooms under the hostel procedure for safety, maintenance, or investigation. Where advance notice is practicable, it should be provided according to the applicable procedure.

The Hostel Office may publish operational instructions consistent with this handbook. Students should follow the latest applicable operational notice while recognizing that a temporary instruction does not automatically amend a permanent handbook rule.

Residents must use laundry and common facilities according to posted schedules. Equipment should be left clean and available for other residents. Damage caused by misuse may be referred under the residence discipline procedure.
Study rooms are shared facilities. Residents may be required to reserve them when demand is high. Personal belongings should not be left unattended for extended periods.

Hostel internet is provided for academic and ordinary personal use subject to technology-use rules. Deliberate network disruption, unauthorized access, or attempts to bypass security controls may be referred to the relevant authority.
A resident should report plumbing, electrical, furniture, or safety problems through the designated maintenance channel. Emergency faults should be reported immediately to hostel staff or security.
Students are responsible for assigned keys or access credentials. Lost keys should be reported promptly. Replacement charges may apply where the residence schedule provides for them.
Students who will be away overnight should use the approved leave process. A parent or friend informing another resident does not constitute official leave approval.
Visitors may be asked to provide identification and comply with security procedures. Residents are responsible for the conduct of visitors they sponsor.
Residents organizing gatherings must comply with quiet-hour and event requirements. Approval for an event on a particular date does not permanently change ordinary residence rules.
Students should report serious injuries, fire hazards, and urgent safety issues through designated channels. Staff may take temporary measures to protect residents.
During an evacuation, students must follow instructions from security and hostel staff and proceed to the designated assembly area. Personal belongings should not delay evacuation.
Food stored in rooms must be kept in a manner consistent with hygiene and hostel safety requirements. Perishable food should not be stored where it creates a sanitation problem.
A resident may submit a complaint concerning facilities or conduct through the designated office. The complaint should identify the issue and relevant dates where possible.
The Hostel Office may issue temporary operational notices for maintenance, examinations, festivals, or security events. Such notices should identify their period of operation.

Students should distinguish permanent handbook rules from temporary operational instructions. When two provisions genuinely conflict and neither states which controls, the resident should seek clarification rather than assume that the later or more convenient rule applies.

This policy explains procedures for students who experience documented medical circumstances or other exceptional situations that affect attendance, examinations, or academic deadlines. It does not create an automatic exemption for every personal difficulty.

Medical grounds may include hospitalization, serious illness, acute injury, or another condition supported by acceptable medical documentation. The Institute may request clarification when a certificate does not establish the period of incapacity or appears incomplete.

A medical certificate should identify the student, relevant dates, issuing medical practitioner or institution, and date of issue. Supporting records may be requested where necessary.

Students should submit medical documents through the official channel. A document submitted informally to a classmate or unrelated office should not be assumed to constitute a valid request.

A student seeking attendance consideration on medical grounds must submit the prescribed request to the department. The department reviews the attendance record and documentation and forwards the recommendation to the designated authority.

**Intentional evaluation provision:** Where a medical exemption is formally approved, this policy states that the student may be treated as eligible for the semester-end examination with attendance of **65% or above**.

The approval should be recorded before the student is treated as eligible under the medical exemption. The provision does not state that every medical certificate automatically produces an exemption.

A student unable to attend an examination because of hospitalization or another documented medical emergency may request a deferred examination. The request should normally be submitted within three working days after the missed examination unless the student was medically incapable of submitting it.

The request should identify the missed examination and include the required documentation. Approval is determined under the applicable procedure.

Exceptional circumstances may include circumstances specifically recognized by an institutional notice or committee decision. Serious medical emergencies and institute-representative obligations may qualify when the relevant process applies.

This policy does not establish an automatic academic exemption for family weddings, vacations, ordinary travel, celebrations, or convenience.

The department verifies the student's course, attendance percentage, and documentation. It may request clarification. The department's recommendation is forwarded to the designated authority when approval is required.

The Exceptional Circumstances Committee may review cases referred by departments. Its decision should identify the provision considered and the relief granted. A decision for one student does not automatically amend a general policy.
Medical consideration may be available for an academic deadline when the relevant policy permits an extension. A medical certificate alone does not automatically extend every Institute deadline.
A student may appeal a rejection when the applicable process provides an appeal. The appeal should identify the original request and explain why reconsideration is requested.
The Institute may verify medical documentation where necessary. False or materially misleading documentation may be referred under the Student Code of Conduct.

Medical records should be submitted through designated channels and handled according to institutional privacy procedures. Students should avoid sending sensitive records to public mailing lists or unrelated offices.

Approved exceptions should record the student, course or activity, relevant period, applicable provision, decision, and approving authority. Records should be sufficient for later administrative verification.

A request based solely on convenience, personal travel, family functions, or social events should not be treated as a medical request. Students should identify another applicable policy if one exists.

This policy should be read together with Academic Regulations. Where provisions appear inconsistent and no explicit precedence rule is provided, the student should seek an institutional determination rather than assume that one document automatically overrides another.

Students should receive acknowledgement of a submitted request through the designated administrative process where such acknowledgement is provided. Students should retain the acknowledgement and decision.
A late request may be considered when the student can establish a reason for delay and the applicable authority has discretion to accept it. Late submission does not guarantee approval.

The purpose of this policy is to provide a documented route for genuine medical and exceptional circumstances while preserving academic procedures. Students should rely on an approved decision rather than on informal assurances.

Medical leave may affect attendance in lectures, laboratories, or other activities only through the approved process. Approval for examination absence does not automatically excuse attendance in every course. The decision should identify the relevant activity where possible.

Where hospitalization prevents a student from making a timely request, the student or an authorized representative may contact the designated office when practicable. Evidence of the hospitalization period may be requested later. Hospitalization does not automatically determine the outcome of an academic assessment.

A temporary injury may support a request for reasonable academic consideration when the relevant process permits it. The student should provide documentation identifying the period during which participation was affected. The Institute may distinguish between inability to attend and inability to complete a particular activity.

For complex requests, the Institute may refer documentation to a designated medical authority. The authority may advise whether documentation supports the claimed period. The academic decision remains subject to the applicable policy and approving authority.
The Institute may verify documentation where necessary. A student should not alter a medical certificate. Suspected alteration may be handled under the conduct process.

Only personnel who need information for processing a request should access medical documentation. Students should use secure institutional channels and should not circulate medical records unnecessarily.

If a student becomes medically incapacitated immediately before an examination, the student should notify the department or examination office as soon as reasonably possible. Emergency communication does not replace the formal application and documentation process.

When a medical attendance request is approved, the department should record the decision against the relevant course or period. Students should verify the record after processing and report discrepancies.

A committee may consider an exceptional event when another institutional policy grants it authority. This policy does not turn a family function, travel plan, or social obligation into a medical ground.

A student whose medical request is pending should not assume that a shortage list has been automatically changed. The official attendance record should be corrected after an approved decision is communicated.

If a student cannot determine which medical process applies, the student should describe the situation to the designated office without assuming a particular outcome. The office may identify the appropriate procedure.

Medical consideration is evidence-based and case-specific. An automated system should report policy language and approval status rather than infer that a medical certificate guarantees academic relief.
This policy establishes general procedures for Institute-administered scholarships and financial aid. Individual scholarship announcements may contain additional conditions.
Eligibility may depend on academic performance, financial need, programme status, and award-specific conditions. Students should read the terms of the particular award.
Applications must be submitted through the designated portal by the published deadline. Supporting documents should be complete and readable.
Where an award specifies an academic threshold, students must satisfy that threshold for renewal. The threshold may differ between awards.

Some scholarships may include attendance requirements. Students should consult the terms of the individual award rather than assume that the general academic attendance requirement is identical to the scholarship requirement.
Need-based awards may require income or financial documentation. Updated documentation may be requested during renewal.
Renewal is subject to verification of continuing eligibility. Receiving an award in one term does not guarantee renewal in the next term.
An award may be suspended when eligibility conditions are not met, required documents are missing, or an award-specific rule provides for suspension.
Cancellation should follow the procedure specified in the award terms. Where cancellation is based on inaccurate information, the Institute may request an explanation.
Approved amounts are normally credited after verification and administrative processing. This policy does not guarantee a particular banking date unless the award notice states one.
A student may appeal a scholarship decision when the award terms provide an appeal mechanism. The appeal should identify the award and decision.
Students should notify the Financial Aid Office when a material change affects eligibility. The office may reassess the award.
Students must disclose other institutional funding when the application requires it. Some awards may restrict simultaneous funding.
The effect of a failed course depends on the terms of the particular scholarship. This policy does not establish a universal rule that every failed course causes cancellation.

Scholarship recipients remain subject to student conduct rules. A conduct finding affects an award only where the scholarship terms or a competent institutional decision provides for that consequence.
Financial aid records should be retained according to institutional recordkeeping procedures.
Administrative verification, incomplete documents, banking errors, or other processing issues may delay payment. A delay does not by itself establish that an award has been cancelled.
The Scholarship Committee may review applications and appeals within the authority assigned by the award programme. Committee membership does not imply authority to alter unrelated academic rules.
Knowingly providing false financial or academic information may result in rejection, suspension, cancellation, or referral under another applicable procedure.
Questions about a particular award should be resolved using its published terms together with this general policy.

The Financial Aid Office may review applications for completeness before substantive eligibility assessment. Missing information may result in a request for clarification. Students should respond within the period stated in the request.
Where applications exceed available funding, selection may use the criteria stated in the particular scholarship announcement. This general policy does not create a universal ranking formula.
A scholarship programme may maintain a waitlist when permitted by its terms. Placement on a waitlist does not guarantee an award.

An award notice should identify material conditions, amount, period, and renewal requirements. Students should retain the notice because a general scholarship policy may not contain the specific terms of an individual award.
A scholarship deferral is available only when the applicable award terms or an authorized decision permit it. Academic leave does not automatically preserve financial aid.

If a student withdraws from a programme, the effect on financial aid depends on the award terms and applicable withdrawal procedure. The general policy does not prescribe a universal repayment amount.

If an administrative error results in an excess scholarship payment, the Financial Aid Office may contact the student and explain the correction process. Students should not treat an unexpected excess payment as a permanent additional award.

A scholarship announcement may establish deadlines for income certificates, academic records, identity documents, or other evidence. Missing a deadline may delay review or affect eligibility when the terms provide for that consequence.
A review request should identify the original decision and any new information. A review is not necessarily a new application.
If an application and supporting documents contain inconsistent information, the Financial Aid Office may request clarification. The award decision may be delayed until the discrepancy is resolved.
Official scholarship decisions should be communicated through the designated channel. Informal statements by students or unrelated staff should not be treated as final award decisions.
Scholarship eligibility is award-specific. The general policy should be used for general procedures, while the individual award notice supplies additional conditions where applicable.

The Student Code of Conduct describes expected behavior and the general disciplinary process. Specific procedures may apply to academic integrity, hostel conduct, technology use, or other specialized matters.
Students must treat peers, staff, visitors, and service personnel respectfully. Threatening, abusive, or seriously disruptive conduct may be referred under the disciplinary process.
Cheating, unauthorized collaboration, fabrication of records, impersonation, and deliberate misrepresentation in academic work may constitute academic misconduct.
Submitting another person's work as one's own without appropriate acknowledgment may constitute plagiarism. The academic unit may apply its academic integrity procedure.
Unwelcome conduct that materially interferes with another person's safety, participation, or learning environment may be investigated under the applicable procedure.
Students must not deliberately damage Institute property or another person's property. Restitution may be considered where responsibility is established.

Institute computing systems must be used according to technology-use rules. Unauthorized access, deliberate disruption, credential misuse, and misuse of institutional systems may be disciplinary matters.
Students must follow Institute and applicable legal requirements concerning restricted substances. Residence rules may impose additional restrictions.
When a complaint is received, the responsible office may conduct a preliminary review. The student may be asked to provide a statement or relevant information.
A disciplinary committee may consider cases referred under the applicable procedure. The committee may issue findings or recommendations within its authority.
Depending on the applicable rules and severity, outcomes may include warning, restitution, restriction, suspension, or another authorized measure.
Students should receive notice of an allegation and the process being used, subject to the requirements of the applicable procedure.
Appeal rights depend on the decision and procedure. An appeal should identify the decision, grounds, and supporting information.
Academic, hostel, and conduct procedures may operate separately. A hostel decision does not automatically determine an academic outcome unless an applicable academic rule provides a connection.
Knowingly submitting materially false information in an institutional process may itself be a conduct concern.
Retaliation against a person for making a good-faith report or participating in an institutional process is prohibited.
Temporary safety measures may be taken when necessary to protect students or staff. Such measures do not by themselves establish a final disciplinary finding.
Students should cooperate with legitimate institutional processes, keep contact details current, and comply with decisions issued under applicable authority.
Disciplinary records should be maintained according to institutional recordkeeping procedures. Access should be limited according to applicable rules.
Students should consult the specific procedure referenced in a notice for detailed timelines, evidence standards, and appeal mechanisms.

Student organizations must comply with registration, event, safety, and financial procedures applicable to recognized organizations. Organization activity does not exempt individual members from the Code of Conduct.
Students organizing an Institute event may need prior approval for venue, timing, security, or other operational matters. Event approval does not authorize conduct prohibited by another policy.

Where an examination incident is referred for disciplinary review, the student may be informed of the allegation and asked to provide a response under the applicable procedure. Academic consequences may also be determined under academic-integrity rules.

Students must not use institutional accounts to impersonate another person, interfere with services, or obtain unauthorized access. Technical access granted for coursework does not authorize access to unrelated systems.

Relevant records may include written statements, system logs, examination materials, photographs, or other information permitted by the applicable process. Students should follow instructions concerning submission of evidence.
An authorized office may impose a temporary measure where necessary to protect safety or preserve an institutional process. An interim measure should not automatically be treated as a final finding.
Students are expected to respond to legitimate notices and requests under disciplinary procedures. Failure to respond may have consequences only where the applicable procedure provides for them.

A single incident may implicate academic, hostel, and conduct rules. Each authority should apply the procedure within its jurisdiction. One process should not automatically be assumed to decide every consequence.
Where an appeal is available, the applicable notice should identify the deadline and submission channel. A student should retain proof of submission.
A student who makes a good-faith report should not be subjected to retaliation for making the report or participating honestly in a review.
Knowingly fabricating a complaint or evidence may itself constitute a conduct concern. A complaint that is not substantiated is not automatically a false complaint; intent and evidence matter.
The Code of Conduct provides general expectations. For a specific allegation, the relevant specialized procedure and official notice should be consulted rather than relying on a generalized summary.
Students ordinarily require 75% attendance to appear for semester-end examinations.

Medical requests require documentation and approval. The separate medical policy contains a special
attendance provision.

A documented medical emergency may support a deferred examination. Family celebrations and ordinary
vacations are not listed as automatic grounds.

The standard hostel curfew is 10:00 PM under the Hostel Handbook. This summary also states that residents
may enter until 11:00 PM. The documents do not provide a precedence rule resolving the difference.

Students must comply with academic integrity, residence, safety, and respectful-conduct requirements. Serious
matters may be referred to the appropriate committee.

Official academic records are maintained by the Academic Office. Students should report discrepancies through
the designated process and retain evidence.

An official notice may modify a date or operational procedure when it expressly identifies the activity and
effective period.

Students should monitor official notices, retain approvals, and verify important records. Informal statements
should not be treated as amendments.
Students must follow reasonable safety instructions in classrooms, laboratories, hostels, and Institute events.

Requests should be submitted through the channel named in the relevant procedure. A request is not an
approval unless the designated authority communicates an approval.

An appeal is available only where the applicable rule or notice provides an appeal route. Students should follow
the stated deadline and submission method.

This summary is intended to be read together with detailed policies. Where two applicable passages genuinely
conflict, an automated system should show the evidence rather than silently invent a resolution.
